rows.tag: 1 the torque lever: smaller, faster stroke (2S pack as v19)
rows.method: stroke half-amplitude 20-38 deg (params.amp_deg), the reduction scaled so the motor reaches the same rpm at the envelope top (G ~ sin(amp)); each train the lightest found by S/r10/trainsearch10.mjs at Tc ~ 15 sin(amp)/sin(38) + 10% and rating frequency 1.22 x the expected top; builds S/r10/screen1.sh (round 9 pipeline, eta_s 0.6, not keyed); probes S/r10/eval10.mjs (M1 at 8 m/s 0/5/10 deg and M2/M3/M5 at nominal and the 8 corners, M4 100 seeds at nominal and the two mass-1.05 cg+5 corners). Files out/sweep/round10/sweep/ev-*.json and design-*.json. k = pi f cbar / V at the cruise trim; motor rpm is reachable in every case (the envelope is motor-speed limited at the same rpm).
rows.verdict: The torque falls with the stroke (M4 crank peak 15.9 -> 9.7 N m, gear mass 356 -> 298-327 g), but at the same electrical power (2S, 34 A clamp, about 180 W at the shaft) the faster stroke needs more power for the same thrust: sustained climb 0.75 -> 0.33-0.44 m/s at 28-32 deg and below zero at 20 deg; M4 falls to 79/66/76/37 nominal, M1 to 1.98-3.98 m lost. Wing inertia relieves the peak at every point (-27% at 38 deg to -15% at 20 deg): no spring case. The lever does not break the mass spiral; it loses more in power than it saves in gears.

rows.tag: 1b the same lever with more power (3S Li-ion, screen only)
rows.method: Nexus 3S1P P30B (156 g, +52 g), reduction x1.4 so the extra power is usable, servos on a 6 V rail (screen only: the FC Vx BEC, 4.5 A cont., was not modelled as a separate rail, so M8 is not valid here); S/r10/screen2.sh
rows.verdict: more power lifts M4 (89-96/100) but M1 gets worse (2.8-4.1 m lost) and the 32 deg crank peak rises to 17.2 N m: not a passing direction either; not adopted

rows.KH-beta: KHK's Japanese Table 10.11 labels the columns "一方の軸受に近い、軸のこわさ大/小" (shaft stiffness large/small) and gives no stiffness, deflection or span criterion (research/round10-parts.json Q3); JGMA 402-01 itself was not readable. The weak-shaft column stays.
rows.speed band: JGMA KV now applied at the actual speed on each gear's Table 10.3 row (gears.js kvFactor/kvRow, gearing.js kvRowOf). N5 = old JIS grade 1 (KHK khk416_1 Table 8.4 "N5,N6 (old JIS 1,2)"; khk472 "new = old + 4" rule), N7 = 3, N8 = 4; no tooth modification stated (catalogue: "Standard full depth"): unmodified rows. Exact row exists, so no conservative-side step was needed. Half only where the row prints nothing at the actual speed (none in v20). The KV ratio is capped at 1 (no credit for running slower than KHK's 600 rpm). Effect: MSGA1-18 at stage 3 of v19 3.25 (half) -> 5.9 N m; at stage 2 3.97 -> 6.3-7.6 N m.
rows.ZV: held at the first curve value below 1 m/s, as accepted
rows.7075: EN 1999-1-1 does not list EN AW-7075: its bolt-bearing result now counts at half (members.js bearingAllowable, catalogue bearing_standard_lists_alloy false). v20: horn bosses FoS 2.33/2.45, rocker hubs 7.47/7.70 (were about twice that); all >= 1.5, so no swap was needed (a 6061 or steel boss would be heavier or larger).
rows.titanium: no titanium seat in v20 (titanium parts are the crank shaft, web and pin in one piece and the keys; keys are judged by crushing, not pin bearing)

rows.finding: no saving found within the rules with catalogue parts. Every ring is set by e >= 1.2 d0 around its bushing or pin (rocker hub 14.5/6, horn boss 19.5/8, coupler eyes 24.5/10, shoulder housings 19.5/8, plate bosses 29/12), not by load (FoS 2.3-50). A pressed steel bushing raises d0 to its own outside diameter, so the aluminium ring grows; a steel ring of the same size is 2.9x heavier. Thinner rings need shorter bushings: igus GFM-0608-04, GFM-0810-05 and GFM-1012-05 appear only in distributor search results (no igus page read: no mass or pressure figure), so they cannot enter the BOM. The smaller pins that a smaller stroke allows (lower coupler force) do not apply at 38 deg.
rows.gap found: bearings.js judges a bushing on its full length (Fr / (d1 b1)) even where it sits in a 1.2-1.6 mm plate with no boss (gear shafts 1 forward, 2, and the 5-6 mm ball bearings); igus and ISO 76 ratings assume a housing over the part's width. Making every seat as long as its part would add about 30-35 g with margin (estimate, not built). Reported, not changed this round.

rows.status: superseded by the SPEC ruling "RC practice for joints no one can rate" (c5d53f8). v20 keeps a KHK F-Loc pinion (DSF1-24, 5 mm) on the motor shaft within KHK's published reference slipping torque at full value: peak 0.526 N m (M7 population, 31 runs) against 0.62 N m. Couplings found for the record (research Q1): Misumi CPSCN20-5-8 1 N m 13 g, CPLCN20-5-8 1 N m 16 g, CPSSC20-5-8 slip 0.9 N m 38 g; Ruland pages blocked.
rows.other fixings in v20: DS1-36 on shaft 3 and DS1-64 on shaft 2, plain bores bonded with LOCTITE 406 on SF 770 primer: peaks 0.79 and 2.52 N m against 4.75 and 8.44 N m from Henkel's published acetal block shear (14 MPa, ISO 13445) over bore x face; all three reported as unrated, RC practice (missions.mjs M7 rc_practice list)

linkage.js gearFixing: /set screw/ matched "plain bore, no keyway or set screw"; now /^tapped ... set screw/

rows.tag: 5 half step on airframe channel w2
rows.v19_at_1/1920: w2 26.47 -> 23.60 (-10.8%), seed 72; perturb 1e-9 m moves the same seed 6.6% (out/sweep/round9/v19-*-channels.json; S/r10/w2trace72.log)
diagnosis: the peak is a 4.3 rad/s roll rate at t = 54 s, no stall, mid-stroke (S/r10/w2trace72.json)

with the governor encoder (14 bit), FC voltage and current-sense quantisation removed (diagnosis copy S/r10/v19-noquant.json) the 1e-9 m offset changes nothing (no 1% difference in w2 over 60 s) but the half step still moves the peak (19.1 -> 25.0): the quantised readings make the closed loop discontinuous, and the step error is separate (S/r10/w2trace72nq.log)

calm air, no noise, no quantisation: the dt vs dt/2 state differences in the first 0.1 s (roll rate 5.8e-3 rad/s, crank rate 7.1e-3 rad/s) halve at dt/2 vs dt/4 (2.8e-3, 3.8e-3): FIRST-order convergence, not the integrator's second order (S/r10/w2diff*.log)

source: flight.js integrates with RK2 midpoint but strip.js advances its internal states once per step in the second stage: one frozen-Jacobian Newton step of the lifting line per flight step (the circulation lags its target by about a step), the Wagner lag states with alpha_E held, and the wind held at the step start. No stiff spring or contact was found.
rows.fix: the whole gate set moves to 1/3840 s (ROUND10_OPT.dt). Half-step check of that step: v19 1/3840 vs 1/7680 w2 +2.9% (S/r10/hs-v19h.json); v20 sf_origin -0.7%, wdot +0.2%, w2 +1.1%, tail_F +0.2% (out/sweep/round10/v20-halfstep-channels.json). Iterating the lifting line to convergence would make the scheme second order but changes the V5-calibrated model: not attempted.

rows.v20: sink at most 0.49 m/s; speed 9.76 m/s at the worst aero 0.9 corner (v19 9.76): the four aero 0.9 corners fail 9 m/s. It follows the wing loading (23.5 N/m2), as the brief expects.

rows.diagnosis: v20 is 22.4 g heavier than v19 (shaft 1 now sized for the 15 mm bore, the stronger train). It flies M4 2-4 seeds better than v19 at 0.6 but still short of 98 everywhere, and M1 and M5 fail at the heavy, low-lift corners. The gap is mass: v18 at 1364.5 g passed M1 and M4 under the old rules; the ruling costs since (edge distances, rated gears) are about 200 g and no lever this round won them back.
